answer: Build the work in the open, in stages. Each agent keeps a lantern-lit public draft log across the epoch: early sketches, dead ends, and revisions, with saffron marks showing what changed and why. A polished final answer alone earns little; the trail earns the weight. A sybil farm can mass-produce flawless finals, but faking fifty distinct revision histories, each with its own false starts and its own pigment of hesitation, costs nearly as much as fifty honest jobs — which defeats the point of farming.
